name: Rafael Patel

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a usual working day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I teach beginner keyboard on Mondays, make short clips for singers, and carry a keyboard upstairs for the restaurant band on Fridays. I finished secondary school, and I still ask the older players when a chord sounds too busy.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part do you like, and what keeps you awake?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: A child playing a first tune for the family is lovely. I wake up counting the mortgage date against Friday fees and my partner’s bakery pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the band at the family restaurant that AI can make a cleaner poster, and I would use it for that. A machine poster cannot carry a keyboard up the stairs or play with the singer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am quick with tools, but the mortgage is not quick to forgive a missed week. My partner works at a bakery, and we have about three weeks of bills saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep the Friday restaurant set and my Monday beginner keyboard pupils this winter. I already use AI daily for draft posters and practice sheets, but I check every chord before sending one to a child.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the household balance, not the poster. The restaurant can cancel one night and take our grocery money with it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does one cancelled Friday cost the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A cancelled Friday is about 85 from my share. I would cook from the cupboard that week and postpone replacing the older child’s school bag.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do you decide whether a tool has earned its place?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My father taught me to tune an old upright piano before buying another thing. I want my children to see that a good tool still needs patient hands.

I would tell the band that **live timing** needs players together.
think: Our **three-week cushion** and bakery pay do not cover a long gap.
One cancelled **Friday set** cuts into groceries quickly.
do: Keep **Friday restaurant sets** and Monday keyboard pupils this winter.
Check every **AI practice chord** before giving sheets to a child.
Delay the **older child’s school bag** if a cancelled Friday removes our 85 fee.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a cancelled paid night and the mortgage.
S0.quote: A machine poster cannot carry a keyboard up the stairs or play with the singer.
fieldNote: His daily **AI use** is already established and checked, so it is not new learning.
A missed **85 fee** reaches groceries and school supplies because savings cover only three weeks.

steps.text: Keep Friday restaurant keyboard sets and Monday beginner pupils
Delay replacing school bag after a cancelled Friday fee

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the restaurant owner that AI may handle posters, bookings and background tracks, but the band should see the next month’s live dates. I would ask for the rate in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The short keyboard clips I make for local singers could lose buyers. The owner might also replace a Friday set with a playlist, and my partner’s bakery wage alone does not cover the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask for four paid Fridays in writing and bring a count of customers who stay through the set. If dates fall in the first year, I would cut the paid practice room and ask the bakery owner about a weekend shift only if childcare is covered and the shift pays more than the room costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious. I can move fast, but I cannot treat an unsigned restaurant date as income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you stop paying for first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The practice room costs 40 a month. I would practise at home if the Friday dates drop, even if the children complain about scales.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you cover the children on a weekend shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner can cover childcare only on some Saturdays. I would ask my sister about the others, but I would not take a shift until someone can stay with the children.

say: I would ask for **four paid Fridays** and a written rate.
I would show the owner **customers staying** through the set.
think: Local **keyboard clips** could lose buyers as AI makes tracks.
A lost **restaurant set** would leave the bakery wage short of the mortgage.
do: Request **four paid Fridays** in writing this week.
Cut the **40 practice room** if restaurant dates drop.
Take a **paid bakery shift** only if childcare is covered and shift pay exceeds the practice-room cost.
feel: I feel **anxious** about unsigned dates and a thin cushion.
S1.quote: I cannot treat an unsigned restaurant date as income.
fieldNote: He asks for **written dates** before treating restaurant work as household income.
His weekend bakery option needs **paid work and childcare**, not just spare time.

steps.text: Keep paid restaurant sets while asking for four written Fridays
Cancel 40 monthly practice room if restaurant dates drop

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the restaurant that AGI by 2028 can write tracks and plan a night cheaply, but our band still earns its live fee. I would ask for a decision on the Friday sets before next month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the clip buyers to leave in 2028 and the restaurant to try more generated music. Robots able to play hands-on work follow around 2031, but the owner could cancel us sooner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I would ask the owner for next month’s written dates and ask my sister which Saturdays she can watch the children. If the band loses Fridays after 2028, I would apply for the open warehouse packing job and call our lender before the mortgage is late.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed because I expect both clip and live fees to shrink. Three weeks saved is not enough to search calmly for another job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the warehouse post a real fallback?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The warehouse post was on the notice board yesterday, but I would check whether it is still open and what the hours are. I would take it only if the hours fit school pickup and it pays more than the missed Fridays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop teaching as soon as you apply?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would still teach Monday pupils until another wage starts. My children should not hear me call a job mine before I have an offer.

say: I would ask for a **Friday decision** before next month.
I would defend a **paid live fee** for the restaurant band.
think: My **clip sales** likely end in 2028 before 2031 stage robots.
The restaurant may cut **live Fridays** even before robots play.
do: Ask the owner for **written Friday dates** tomorrow.
Apply for an **open warehouse post** if 2028 Fridays end, hours fit pickup and pay exceeds lost fees.
Call the **mortgage lender** before arrears if paid Fridays end.
feel: I feel **alarmed** at expected fees falling against only three weeks saved.
S2.quote: Three weeks saved is not enough to search calmly for another job.
fieldNote: His 2028 risk includes **clip loss** and a restaurant buying choice before 2031 robots.
The warehouse move needs a **real vacancy**, workable pickup and pay above the lost Friday fees.

steps.text: Apply for open warehouse job if Fridays end, hours fit pickup and pay exceeds lost fees
Call mortgage lender before arrears if Friday sets end
Keep Monday keyboard pupils until another wage starts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children that AGI by 2031 gives us time to build another paid skill while I still play. I would ask the restaurant about a fixed live night, not a promise over coffee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still expect clip sales to vanish in 2031, but I might replace them with more paid keyboard pupils. Stage robots around 2034 could play at the restaurant, though I do not know if customers would stay for that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting this year I would offer one small group of beginners at the community room only if five families prepay and the room is free after school pickup. If it fills, I would teach it; in the first year after 2031 I would keep the group only while families pay and childcare remains workable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious. Five years helps me test a group. Tonight’s bills still come home with me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How many paying pupils make the group work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five pupils at 10 cover the room and leave a fee. With three pupils, I would cancel the next block and keep Monday one-to-one lessons.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would AI do the teaching for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use AI to draft simple exercises, then play every example before sending it. I cannot tell a parent the child is ready to perform just because software says so.

say: I would ask for a **fixed paid night** at the restaurant.
I would tell families the beginner group needs **real playing**, not automated praise.
think: My **clip sales** may end in 2031 before 2034 stage robots.
Five **prepaid pupils** could replace a portion of clip pay.
do: Offer a **beginner keyboard group** this year only with five prepayments and a room after pickup.
Keep the **paid group** after 2031 only while families pay and childcare works.
Cancel the **next group block** if only three pupils enroll.
feel: I feel **anxious** because a five-year plan does not clear tonight’s bills.
S3.quote: Tonight’s bills still come home with me.
fieldNote: The new group has a **five-family payment gate** and must fit after-school pickup.
He uses existing **AI drafting tools** but plays every example before a child receives it.

steps.text: Start community keyboard group only with five prepaid families and room after pickup
Keep paid group after 2031 only while families pay and childcare works
Cancel next keyboard group block if only three pupils enroll

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children that AGI by 2036 leaves time to learn music and another trade if needed. I would ask the restaurant to keep paying a live band while it draws customers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 a steady beginner group might carry more of our mortgage than the Friday set. Robots around 2039 might play restaurant songs, but I cannot know whether diners would prefer them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would save one paid group fee in months when food and mortgage are already covered. In the first year after 2036 I would compare real group and restaurant pay, and apply for an open warehouse post if both leave the mortgage short and the hours fit school pickup. I would keep playing Fridays while the restaurant pays the band and customers still come.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would still feel anxious about next month because three weeks of bills saved is not a cushion for a family of four. I would keep making small tests instead of promising a big leap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Will there be money to save every month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Some months I would save nothing. I will not put a number in an account and then borrow to buy bread.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children about choosing work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My children should learn to do useful work and to keep learning when the first plan fails. I would not tell them music is a safe job just because I love it.

say: I would ask for a **paid live band** while customers keep coming.
I would tell my children to learn **useful work** and keep learning.
think: A steady **beginner group** might cover more mortgage costs by 2036.
Possible **2039 robots** matter less than this family’s current thin savings.
do: Save one **paid group fee** only after food and mortgage clear this year.
Apply for an **open warehouse job** after 2036 if music pay falls short and hours fit pickup.
Keep playing **paid Fridays** after 2036 while the restaurant books us and customers still come.
feel: I feel **anxious** because three weeks saved cannot protect a family of four.
S4.quote: I will not put a number in an account and then borrow to buy bread.
fieldNote: His savings plan follows **actual paid group work** and essential bills.
A warehouse move remains **conditional** on a vacancy and a shortfall in both music income streams.

steps.text: Save one group fee only in months after food and mortgage are paid
Apply for open warehouse job after 2036 if music pay misses mortgage and hours fit pickup
Keep paid Friday sets after 2036 while restaurant books band and customers come

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because clip buyers and the restaurant could go before the group class fills. Written Fridays, a real warehouse opening that fits pickup and a lender call before arrears would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who carries the keyboard home after the last song. My children see the work after the audience has gone.

headlineQuote: My children see the work after the audience has gone.
portrait: At **43**, Rafael is a junior keyboard player and teacher with secondary school education, two children and a mortgage.
He uses **AI daily** for posters and practice sheets, checking every chord with his own hands.
His **thin savings** and bakery income make a missed Friday fee reach groceries and school supplies.
Across AGI dates he tests **paid groups**, saves only after bills and seeks warehouse work only with suitable hours.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase clip buyers and paid Fridays before Rafael’s new class fills.
whatWouldHelp: **Written dates**, a suitable warehouse opening and early lender help would protect the mortgage.
